script:
Zhao San
Zhao San was an orphan who had been adopted by the Zhao family and grew up with Zhao Zhongzheng. The Zhao family was a major clan of the Western Gate, and the Western Gate and Eastern Territory had been life-and-death enemies since ancient times. When Zhao Zhongzheng was about ten years old, the old clan leader had a late son, Zhao Zhongyang, who was greatly favored. Zhao Zhongzheng was very jealous of Zhao Zhongyang, which Zhao San observed but didn't dare comment on.
As they grew up, Zhao Zhongzheng displayed extraordinary business talent, earning himself a place in the family, while Zhao Zhongyang, though not a businessman, possessed righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and virtue. Compared to the somewhat scheming Zhao Zhongzheng, he was more popular and had higher prestige—the two were evenly matched. Zhao Zhongzheng coveted the clan leader position and was unwilling to yield.
Zhao San rarely got involved in these major affairs, only helping Zhao Zhongzheng with private matters, as Zhao Zhongzheng still trusted him greatly. Besides this, Zhao San sought money for himself. Zhao Zhongyang had a subordinate named Zhang Wei, also greedy for money, and the two used their positions as trusted associates of the Zhao family's young masters to profit considerably.
One day, Zhang Wei and Zhao San went drinking together. Zhang Wei complained that Zhao Zhongyang was too demanding of him. The previous time Zhang Wei had taken someone's money to speak well of them in front of Zhao Zhongyang, Zhao Zhongyang instead scolded him, saying he was greedy and would eventually be harmed by it. Zhao San was also contemptuous—these wealthy young masters didn't understand their hardships.
In May 1507, Zhao San received a business opportunity to sell a prosperous Western Market shop owned by the Zhao family to Boss Ma, who offered 20,000 taels to bribe him. Since this shop was under Zhao Zhongyang's management, he approached Zhang Wei, told him about the deal, and asked him to make arrangements, agreeing to split the profits 40-60 with Zhang Wei taking the larger share. However, Zhang Wei was reluctant, saying Zhao Zhongyang was watching this shop closely and he couldn't make this decision. Zhao San had no choice but to abandon the plan.
At the end of June that same year, Zhao Zhongzheng approached Zhao San with 200,000 silver taels, saying that to ensure he smoothly obtained the clan leader position, he wanted Zhao San to kill Zhao Zhongyang. Zhao San didn't dare agree. Zhao Zhongzheng then said he would give another 1 million taels after the deed was done. This time Zhao San was truly tempted—with that money, he could escape anywhere and live luxuriously for the rest of his life.
Zhao San thought of many ways to kill Zhao Zhongyang but found them all impractical, so he decided on the simplest method—stabbing him to death. He went to the market, bought a dagger, prepared a pot of poison, and boiled the dagger in it for three days, planning to use this to deal with Zhao Zhongyang.
[Night of July 25th]
That night, Zhao San dressed in black, put on a mask, and came to Zhao Zhongyang's courtyard just before 11 PM. He quietly pushed open the door and entered. The courtyard was very dark, but Zhao Zhongyang's room was lit with two people inside—presumably him and his lover Chen Meier. Since they weren't yet married, clan rules forbade them from cohabitating, so Zhao San wasn't in a hurry and waited in the darkness. But soon, someone suddenly lunged at him, punching him dizzy. Shaking his head, Zhao San fought back. This person took the beating without calling for help or even making a sound, just fighting and trying to drive him out. When Zhao San pulled out his dagger to stab him, the man knocked it away with a palm strike, and the dagger disappeared into the darkness. After about 10 minutes, Zhao San was exhausted and couldn't continue fighting—he had no idea where this madman had come from—so he fled. The man didn't pursue him.
acts_goal: Don't actively expose that Zhao Zhongzheng bribed him to kill Zhao Zhongyang.
